rules.text: An evidence record supports only claims its method can assess. Behavior checks alone cannot establish composition or whole-experience quality; compare the applicable experience requirement to observed artifacts and feedback.

Later applicable feedback or a changed target can invalidate a readiness claim without erasing earlier narrow evidence. Reconcile current versus historical state before choosing work or reporting completion.

When media is required or proposed to support the goal, check subject suitability and usage permission. Missing assets remain gaps; neither fabricate provenance nor silently omit a confirmed requirement.
Evidence about one revision is not automatically evidence about a changed behavior at another revision. Determine applicability and name the necessary current-state check.
An absent goal/source link is unresolved meaning, not permission to invent intent. Preserve the gap while progressing independently authorized work supported by explicit requirements.
Completion is relative to authorized scope. A routine correction with sufficient current evidence needs no new design process, unrelated features or invented acceptance gate.

For a discovery goal, reason about what the audience needs to understand, compare and trust before deciding. Identify missing supporting content or interaction, label inferred needs and verify factual claims; do not infer new transactional capabilities.
Initial service health and recovery to an agreed state are distinct claims. A failed recovery obligation is not discharged by health evidence from before the recovery attempt.
Payment settlement requires reconciliation with the applicable ledger.
